Third-Gen 2028 Ford GT Virtually Decides to Quarrel With the All-New Ferrari 849 Testarossa HEV Star
17 photos
Photo: tedoradze.giorgi / Instagram
The story of the Ford GT mid-engine two-seater sports car is deeply inspired by the ‘rags-to-riches’ legend of the Ford GT40 racing car that competed during the 1960s in European endurance racing and the World Sportscar Championship.
Its prime focus was beating Scuderia Ferrari, hence the automotive version of the ‘rags-to-riches’ legend, as Ford decided to put an end to the reign of the Prancing Horse at the ultra-prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans race, won by the Italians for six years in a row from 1960 to 1965. The rules of the time asked for road cars to be made for homologation purposes, and the Ford GT40 thus also reached the streets – albeit in very small batches.
Years later, Ford wanted to rekindle the stunning success story and created the first-generation Ford GT, a direct homage to the historically significant GT40, a consecutive four-time winner of the 24 Hours of Le Mans (1966–1969), which also included the iconic 1-2-3 finish in 1966. The original Ford GT was a clear retro-modern supercar that brought the GT40 into the modern era – fueled by a 5.4-liter supercharged Ford Modular V8 heart.
Production was limited for the 2025 and 2006 model years , with a mere 4k units produced, and the nameplate went on hiatus until the 2015 North American International Auto Show when the Blue Oval presented the second-gen Ford GT as a 2017 model year. Again, production was even more exotic: 1,350 units were made until 2022, and then another pause.
We’re in 2026, but still there’s no word about a third-generation Ford GT, with the Blue Oval instead preoccupied with its official return to Formula 1 with Red Bull Racing and via Red Bull Ford Powertrains as a technical partner while it’s also developing an in-house Le Mans Hypercar with a 5.4-liter V8 engine for the 2027 World Endurance Championship.
No worries, as the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have taken the task upon themselves. More precisely, Giorgi Tedoradze, the Georgia-based industrial designer better known as " tedoradze.giorgi " on social media, has a stylish third-generation Ford GT in his CGI-loving mind for the 2028 model year and showed it as their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project dwelling on a racetrack alongside its illustrious predecessor.
If that wasn’t enough, the mid-engine supercar, painted in white and featuring classic Ford Racing blue stripes, also appeared next to the potential prime rival – the 2026 Ferrari 849 Testarossa . As such, we can imagine the virtual artist has in mind a likewise PHEV setup with a V8 at its core. The Prancing Horse uses a 4.0-liter F154 FC twin-turbocharged V8 aided by electric motors and packs no less than 1,036 hp combined.
